title: The Iowa Lead Detonation Happened. Now the Real Work Begins to Study It
summary:
On Wednesday morning, the US Army detonated nearly five tons of degraded lead azide outside of Middletown, Iowa.
Air, soil, and water samples they’ve collected will determine the extent of lead exposure, if any, in Middletown and the surrounding area.
Poor communication between the Army and towns in the path of the fallout led to a public uproar.
Several departments at the University of Iowa kicked into gear to begin to set up air and soil monitoring stations late last week.
Scientists at Purdue University, nearly 300 miles away, also put out a call for soil samples from Middletown.

title: William D. Nordhaus obituary: economist whose tools transformed climate policy
summary:
Credit: Monica Jorge/New York Times/Redux/eyevineWilliam (Bill) Nordhaus was an economist known for introducing climate change into economic analysis, earning him the 2018 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.
His research shaped our understanding of what drives economic growth and innovation.
He realized that omitting the environment from economic measurement would send the wrong signals about the directions of economic growth and, therefore, pioneered more-inclusive ways to measure growth.
Why we need an International Panel on InequalityNext, he questioned the nature of economic growth.
GNP also understates some of the benefits of economic growth, such as increased household well-being, from inventions such as electricity and home appliances.

title: Fast Fashion Fiasco: Shein to Pay $100 Million in FTC Complaint
summary:
The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase issues and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.
In 2026, the company is estimated to ship roughly 1 million packages to US customers daily, according to the FTC.
That number becomes even more astounding when you consider that Shein, the FTC alleges, employed just five customer service agents to answer calls from American customers.
According to Yale Climate Connections, the company emitted 16.7 million total metric tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere in 2023.
Shein has since pledged to improve its treatment of workers and reduce carbon emissions, but scrutiny persists.

title: Thanksgiving Travel Will Be a Stormy Mess
summary:
Expect travel headaches from coast to coast this week.
Several rounds of disruptive weather sweep are likely to cause delays at airports and make for challenging driving conditions just in time for the Thanksgiving long weekend.
Potent systems rolling into the West Coast will bring disruptions from Seattle to San Francisco, where high tides could swamp airport runways.
The stormy setup arrives at the peak travel time of the year in the US.
And with the extreme weather this week is set to sweep across some of the country’s biggest travel hubs, it could upend the best-laid travel plans.

title: As food prices rise, do shoppers still care about sustainability?
summary:
One economist told Bloomberg that Americans should expect food prices to keep creeping up into next year.
With food prices creeping up, it’s worth asking whatever happened to the idea of consumers as climate or environmental activists.
But do today’s shoppers still care about where their food comes from and how it’s grown when they’re worried about their supermarket bill (and all the other ones)?
“People want a sustainable option.
Real change may come when policy changes and public investment in sustainable food systems matches consumer desires, said Jody Kirchner, director of market insights at Good Food Institute, a think tank focused on the alternative protein economy.

title: Urgent action needed to protect Buttermere, new reports warns
summary:
Tourism, infrastructure challenges and "outdated, undersized and poorly maintained" wastewater systems are contributing to the ecological decline of a popular lake, an environmental group has warned.
Buttermere, in the Lake District, has seen rising nutrient levels in recent years which can lead to excess phosphorus and blankets of algae.
West Cumbria Rivers Trust (WCRT), a charity which tracked down the sources of phosphorus for the study, argues "urgent regulatory action and maintenance guidance are needed".
The Buttermere Nutrient Investigations Project was commissioned and funded by the Environment Agency (EA) after the lake was last year found to be failing to meet total phosphorus targets.
WCRT said the investigation showed Buttermere - a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest and Special Area of Conservation - was a "fragile ecosystem under pressure".

title: Pollution Driven by U.S. Data Centers Causing Hundreds of Early Deaths
summary:
U.S. data centers are driving greater power demand, and with it, more pollution from coal and gas power plants.
The new modeling study finds that, in 2023, the added power demand from data centers led to an estimated 650 early deaths across the U.S.
Given the rapid buildout of data centers, their impact would likely be even greater today, authors say.
The study further suggests that pollution is often intensifying far from where data centers are located.
In Oregon and Virginia, two data center hotspots, they are consuming more than 15 percent of the electricity sold in each state.
